Apple pruning: stop dieback, shading and weak buds

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Bad pruning is behind much of the dieback, weak buds and alternate bearing in Indian orchards. Use thinning cuts instead of heading cuts, remove limbs thicker than half the trunk with angled renewal cuts, bend branches to 45–60°, cut 15 cm below any canker with sterilised tools, and immediately paste every cut over 2.5 cm with copper oxychloride or Bordeaux paste (ICAR, SKUAST-K).

What goes wrong with heavy pruning

  • Heading cuts (cutting branch tips back) produce bunches of upright, non-fruiting shoots.
  • Vigorous upper tiers shade the lower branches, so lower spurs do not form flower buds: weak flowering and on-year/off-year bearing.
  • Narrow forks under 30° split under crop load.
  • Unsealed stubs and large cuts let Botryosphaeria and Diplodia canker in; limbs then die back, and growers call them "dead-like plants".

Winter (dormant) pruning, step by step

  1. Remove dead, diseased and broken wood first. Cut cankers 15 cm into healthy green wood.
  2. Sterilise tools between trees with 70% ethanol.
  3. Thin out, do not head back: remove whole limbs that are more than half the trunk's thickness with an angled renewal cut that leaves a short stub to regrow.
  4. Keep the top narrower than the bottom so light reaches lower spurs (tall spindle or modified leader shape).
  5. Bend young branches to 45–60° (beyond horizontal in tall spindle systems) instead of cutting them.
  6. Paste every cut over 2.5 cm the same day with copper oxychloride or Bordeaux paste. Old Chaubattia paste contains red lead; prefer lead-free copper paste.
  7. Whitewash trunks in November against sunscald and canker.

Summer pruning

In July–August remove upright water sprouts that shade fruit. This lets light colour the fruit naturally and reduces the need for colour sprays.

Training systems

SystemRootstockShape
Open centre / modified leaderSeedling, MM.111Wide tree, few scaffold limbs
Spindle bushMM.106, MM.111, M.7Central leader with short, renewed fruiting branches
Vertical axis / tall spindleM.9 on trellisNarrow, tall leader; many small branches bent below horizontal and renewed regularly

Questions farmers ask

When should apple trees be pruned?

Main pruning in winter dormancy (December–February), plus light summer pruning of water sprouts in July–August.

What should I apply on apple pruning cuts?

Copper oxychloride or Bordeaux paste on every cut over 2.5 cm, the same day. Prefer lead-free paste to old Chaubattia paste.

Why do apple branches dry after pruning?

Usually canker (Botryosphaeria, Diplodia) entering through unsealed cuts or stubs. Cut 15 cm into healthy wood, sterilise tools and paste the cut.

Does pruning cause alternate bearing?

Heavy heading cuts and shaded lower branches reduce flower buds and feed the on-year/off-year cycle. Thinning cuts and an open canopy help.
